chunks: And al-Imad al-Hanbali said in Shadharat al-Dhahab, Vol. 3, p. 199:

al-Mufid, Abu Abdallah Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Nu'man al-Baghdadi al-Karkhi, also known as Ibn al-Mu'allim — the scholar of the Shia, the imam of the Rafidah, and the author of numerous compilations.

key_terms.الرَّافِضَةِ: al-Rafidah — a polemical Sunni designation for Shia Muslims, used here by the Hanbali author
key_terms.الشِّيعَةِ: the Shia — partisans of the Ahlulbayt
key_terms.الْمُفِيدُ: al-Mufid ('the Beneficial One') — honorific title of Muhammad ibn al-Nu'man al-Baghdadi, foremost Shia theologian and jurist (d. 413 AH)

ai.seo_question: What title did the Sunni Hanbali historian Ibn al-Imad al-Hanbali give to Sheikh al-Mufid in Shadharat al-Dhahab?
ai.summary: The Hanbali Sunni historian Ibn al-Imad al-Hanbali records in Shadharat al-Dhahab (Vol. 3, p. 199) that al-Mufid — Abu Abdallah Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Nu'man al-Baghdadi al-Karkhi, also known as Ibn al-Mu'allim — was the scholar of the Shia, the imam of the Rafidah, and the prolific author of numerous compilations. This entry represents a notable cross-sectarian acknowledgment by a Sunni historian of al-Mufid's towering intellectual stature in the Islamic scholarly tradition.
